title: The affine torsion cohomological dimension bound
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $c\ge0$ an integer with $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\le c$. For any nonempty affine finite-type $K$-scheme $X$,
$$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\le\dim X+c,$$
with bounds understood as in [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] and Krull dimension as in [def-kun-dimension]. If $X$ is empty, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge0$.

proof.text: Work with bounded-exponent sheaves using the existing source reduction. Additivity preserves the positive annihilator under finite direct image; the finite edge-map bijection transfers a cohomological bound. Finite injective Noether normalization reduces affine finite-type schemes to polynomial spaces with the number of variables bounded by their dimension. Treat a zero coordinate ring as an empty spectrum.

Strongly induct simultaneously over all fields and all available field cohomological bounds. Descend from algebraic closure by the source ground-field theorem and the already proved field-base-change dimension inequality. Polynomial spaces of dimension zero are isomorphic to the field spectrum; dimension one uses the proved source affine-curve bound. For dimension n+2 apply the polynomial induction-step theorem with the simultaneous smaller-dimensional induction hypotheses.

Finite type supplies a finite natural upper bound on topologicalKrullDim X. Hence unbotD 0 is not infinity, and ENat.natCast_toNat together with WithBot.le_coe_unbotD makes its toNat a natural upper bound on dimension. Apply the simultaneous induction with this bound and compare Sheaf.H to the derived-category cohomology in the unchanged target signature. This argument does not need the Nonempty hypothesis. For an empty scheme geometric points detect every sheaf as zero and all its cohomology, including degree zero, vanishes.

proof_origin.place: Finite normalization, simultaneous all-fields induction, polynomial projection/support Leray argument, empty clause
